subject: English
description: Direct ↔ indirect speech — tense-shift rules, modal/pronoun changes, time/place expressions, statements/questions/commands.

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: 'He said, "I am happy."'

options.option_text: He said that he was happy
He said that I am happy here
He says that he is happy now
He told that I was happy here

questions.explanation: DIRECT → INDIRECT (REPORTED) speech RULES: (1) PRONOUNS shift to maintain reporter's perspective: 'I' → 'he/she' (depending on speaker's gender). (2) TENSE shifts BACK if reporting verb is in PAST tense: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; present perfect → past perfect; past simple → past perfect. (3) Add 'THAT' (often optional in indirect statements). (4) Remove QUOTES. EXAMPLE: 'He said, "I am happy"' → 'He said THAT he WAS happy.' KEY TENSE SHIFT TABLE: (a) am/is/are → was/were. (b) do/does → did. (c) was/were → had been. (d) have/has → had. (e) had → had. (f) will → would. (g) shall → should/would. (h) can → could. (i) may → might. (j) must → had to (or unchanged). EXCEPTIONS to tense shift (when truth is universal/eternal): (1) Universal facts: 'He said that the sun rises in the east' (no shift, 'rises' — universal truth). (2) Habitual actions in present: sometimes preserved. WHEN reporting verb is PRESENT: 'He says, "I am happy"' → 'He says (that) he is happy' (no tense shift). PRACTICE: 'They said, "We will come"' → 'They said they WOULD come.' (NOT 'will'). PYQ FREQUENCY: direct/indirect basic conversion in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert: 'She said, "I will go to the market tomorrow."'

options.option_text: She said that she would go to the market the next day
She said that she will go tomorrow market here
She said she is going to market today (not this)
She said that I would go market tomorrow (not this)

questions.explanation: TWO CHANGES: (1) WILL → WOULD (modal shift in indirect). (2) TOMORROW → THE NEXT DAY (time-expression shift). KEY TIME/PLACE EXPRESSIONS that change in REPORTED SPEECH: (a) NOW → THEN. (b) TODAY → THAT DAY. (c) TOMORROW → THE NEXT DAY / THE FOLLOWING DAY. (d) YESTERDAY → THE PREVIOUS DAY / THE DAY BEFORE. (e) THIS → THAT. (f) THESE → THOSE. (g) HERE → THERE. (h) AGO → BEFORE. (i) LAST week/month → THE PREVIOUS week/month. (j) NEXT week/month → THE FOLLOWING week/month. SAMPLE: 'He said, "I bought it yesterday"' → 'He said he had bought it the day before.' ANOTHER: 'She said, "I am here now"' → 'She said she was there then.' KEY TENSE SHIFT for MODALS: (1) will → would. (2) shall → should. (3) can → could. (4) may → might. (5) must → had to (or unchanged for general moral obligation). PRACTICE: 'He said, "I can swim"' → 'He said he could swim.' 'She said, "You must come"' → 'She said I had to come / he must come' (depends). FUTURE-IN-PAST: 'would' is the past form of 'will' — used when REPORTING a future-tense statement IN THE PAST. PYQ FREQUENCY: time-expression shifts in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains, RBI English 1× per cycle.
questions.subject: English

options.option_text: She asked where I lived
She asked where do I live there
She asked that I lived where then
She told me where I lived right then

questions.explanation: REPORTED QUESTION rules: (1) Use 'asked', 'inquired' (NOT 'said'). (2) For WH-QUESTIONS (who, what, where, when, why, how): keep WH-WORD + change tense + reorder to STATEMENT structure (no auxiliary inversion). 'Where do you live?' → 'where I lived' (WH + subject + verb; do dropped, tense shifted). (3) For YES/NO QUESTIONS (no WH-word): use 'IF' or 'WHETHER'. 'Are you coming?' → 'asked if I was coming.' KEY: NO QUESTION MARK in indirect; statement form. NO AUXILIARY 'do/does/did' (it's absorbed into tense shift). EXAMPLES: (1) 'He asked, "What is your name?"' → 'He asked what my name was.' (2) 'She asked, "Will you help?"' → 'She asked if I would help.' (3) 'They asked, "Where are we going?"' → 'They asked where they were going.' (4) 'I said, "Have you eaten?"' → 'I asked if she/he had eaten.' KEY TRAPS: (a) Don't keep 'do/does/did' in indirect: WRONG: 'asked where do I live'. (b) Don't add 'that': WRONG: 'asked that where I lived'. (c) Don't keep '?': WRONG: 'asked where I lived?' INDIRECT QUESTIONS take period (.), not question mark. PYQ FREQUENCY: WH-question conversion in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert imperatives: 'The teacher said, "Open your books."'

options.option_text: The teacher told us to open our books
The teacher said that we open the books
The teacher told that we should open books
The teacher asked open the books

questions.explanation: IMPERATIVE → INDIRECT speech: use 'TOLD/ORDERED/COMMANDED + object + TO + base verb'. 'Open your books' → 'told us to OPEN our books'. KEY: (1) Use 'TO + base verb' (infinitive). (2) PRONOUNS shift (your → our). (3) Choose appropriate REPORTING VERB based on tone: (a) NEUTRAL: 'told' (most common). (b) AUTHORITATIVE: 'ordered', 'commanded', 'demanded'. (c) ADVISORY: 'advised', 'suggested', 'recommended'. (d) REQUEST: 'requested', 'asked'. (e) PROHIBITIVE: 'forbade', 'told NOT TO'. (f) WARNING: 'warned'. PRACTICE: (1) 'Stop!' → 'told me to stop' / 'commanded me to stop'. (2) 'Please come early' → 'requested me to come early.' (3) 'Don't be late' → 'told me not to be late' / 'warned me against being late.' (4) 'Help your sister' → 'asked me to help my sister.' (5) 'Always speak the truth' → 'advised me to always speak the truth.' NEGATIVE IMPERATIVES: 'Don't smoke' → 'told me NOT TO smoke' OR 'forbade me to smoke.' KEY: TO + V1 structure for imperatives. SUGGESTIONS: 'Let's go' → 'suggested going' or 'proposed that we should go.' EXAM TRAP: students mistakenly say 'told me that I should open' — INCORRECT for imperative; should use TO + V1. PYQ FREQUENCY: imperative conversion in SSC CGL, IBPS PO English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert exclamations: 'He said, "What a beautiful sunset!"'

options.option_text: He exclaimed that the sunset was beautiful
He said what a beautiful sunset there
He exclaimed the sunset is very beautiful
He told that the beautiful sunset was here

questions.explanation: EXCLAMATIONS → INDIRECT speech: use 'EXCLAIMED' (or 'cried out', 'shouted') + 'that' + adjective transformed into normal form. PATTERN: 'What a/an + ADJ + N!' → 'exclaimed that the/a + N + was/were + ADJ.' EXAMPLE: 'What a beautiful sunset!' → 'exclaimed that the sunset was beautiful.' KEY TRANSFORMATION: (1) REPORTING VERB: 'said' → 'exclaimed' (or 'said with joy/sorrow/surprise', etc.). (2) DROP exclamation words: WHAT, HOW, ALAS, OH, WOW. (3) USE 'THAT' to introduce. (4) RESTRUCTURE: '(adj) + (noun)' → '(noun) + was/were + (adj)'. PRACTICE: (1) 'Hurrah! We won!' → 'shouted joyfully that they had won.' (2) 'Alas! He is dead.' → 'lamented that he was dead.' (3) 'How tall the building is!' → 'exclaimed that the building was very tall.' (4) 'Oh! It's raining' → 'exclaimed that it was raining.' KEY EMOTIONAL VERBS for exclamation: (a) JOY: rejoiced, shouted with joy, exclaimed joyfully. (b) SORROW: lamented, mourned, regretted. (c) SURPRISE: exclaimed with surprise, cried out. (d) FEAR: cried out in fear, screamed. (e) PRAISE: applauded, praised. EXAM-FAVOURITE: pick reporting verb that captures EMOTIONAL TONE of original exclamation. PYQ FREQUENCY: exclamation conversion in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO English 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert: 'He said, "The earth revolves around the sun."'

options.option_text: He said that the earth revolves around the sun
He said that the earth revolved around the sun
He told the earth had revolved sun (not this)
He said earth was revolving around sun

questions.explanation: EXCEPTION to TENSE-SHIFT RULE: When the reported speech expresses a UNIVERSAL TRUTH, SCIENTIFIC FACT, or HABITUAL ACTION (eternally true), TENSE DOES NOT SHIFT. 'The earth revolves around the sun' is a permanent astronomical fact — KEEP 'revolves' in present tense. KEY EXCEPTIONS to tense shift: (1) UNIVERSAL TRUTHS: 'Sun rises in the east' — present continues. (2) SCIENTIFIC FACTS: 'Water boils at 100°C' — present. (3) PROVERBS: 'Honesty is the best policy' — present. (4) HISTORICAL FACTS (sometimes; debated): 'India became independent in 1947' — usually past simple OK either way. (5) MATHEMATICAL FACTS: 'Two plus two equals four' — present. (6) HABITUAL ACTIONS in present (sometimes): 'I exercise daily.' SAMPLE — exam variations: (a) 'He said, "Honesty is the best policy"' → 'He said that honesty IS the best policy' (NOT 'was'). (b) 'She said, "Boiling point of water is 100°C"' → present preserved. (c) 'Galileo said, "The earth moves"' → present preserved (universal). EXAM-FAVOURITE TRAP: students mechanically apply tense shift, missing the universal-truth exception. WHEN UNCERTAIN: if the statement holds eternally, KEEP present; if it's a momentary observation, SHIFT to past. PYQ FREQUENCY: universal-truth exception in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO English 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Convert: 'They said, "We bought a car last month."'

options.option_text: They said that they had bought a car the previous month
They said that we bought a car last month here
They said they bought car some month ago there
They told that we will buy a car next month here

questions.explanation: TWO MAIN CHANGES: (1) PAST SIMPLE 'bought' → PAST PERFECT 'had bought' (tense shift). (2) 'LAST MONTH' → 'THE PREVIOUS MONTH' (time-expression shift). PRONOUN: 'we' (refers to 'they' the speakers in this case) → 'they'. KEY TENSE SHIFTS for past tenses: (1) PAST SIMPLE → PAST PERFECT: 'I went' → 'he had gone'. (2) PAST CONTINUOUS → PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS: 'I was eating' → 'he had been eating'. (3) PAST PERFECT → PAST PERFECT (no further shift, already perfect): 'I had finished' → 'he had finished'. (4) PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS → no further shift. PRESENT TENSE SHIFTS: (1) PRESENT SIMPLE → PAST SIMPLE: 'I work' → 'he worked'. (2) PRESENT CONTINUOUS → PAST CONTINUOUS: 'I am working' → 'he was working'. (3) PRESENT PERFECT → PAST PERFECT: 'I have worked' → 'he had worked'. SAMPLE: 'I have lived here for 10 years' → 'he had lived there for 10 years.' KEY EXCEPTIONS: when the situation is STILL TRUE / RECENTLY TRUE: '(a) She said, "I am pregnant"' → if she's still pregnant, may keep 'I am' — but most exams shift to 'was'. (b) Universal truths — no shift. PYQ FREQUENCY: complex multi-shift problems in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains, RBI English 1-2× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests systematic application of multiple rules.
